correctness.rationale: For k>=2 the compulsory edge imbalances are exactly -1 at N_i and +1 at P_i (1<=i<=k-2). Any balancing flow decomposes into paths from N_i to P_j, and a path from N_i needs >=i shifts before its vertex can begin with zero, proving >=sum_i i extra edges even for arbitrary hosts. Equality forces j=i by suffix-zero overlap, and then appending exactly i ones. These forced paths balance a strongly connected mandatory graph, giving an optimal Euler circuit. The BEST formula for rooted circuits with designated 0^k edge reduces to t_Z because every outdegree is <=2. An in-tree cannot select append-one at any N_i without a directed cycle; then each P_i gives an independent binary choice, hence t_Z=2^(k-2). All cases k>=2, including k=2, are addressed. Packaged verifier independently corroborates exact constructions, assignment minima, rooted Eulerian counts and bounded exhaustive host enumeration.

originality.rationale: Primary literature on forbidden-language de Bruijn sequences and universal cycles was compared by mathematical implication, including the distinction between linearly one-run compulsory windows and circularly one-run complete Eulerian spectra, and between exact universal cycles and unrestricted shortest covers. No inspected source gives the sharp unrestricted quadratic optimum together with the forced completion and 2^(k-2) complete optimum multiplicity. This is best-knowledge originality, not an absolute uniqueness certification.

value.rationale: The natural compulsory language comprises all length-k binary words with one linear run of ones. Its minimal cyclic completion is not obvious because arbitrary extra windows are allowed; the proof establishes an exact quadratic optimum, identifies uniquely every forced extra window, and classifies/counts all shortest cyclic hosts for every k. This is a complete structural covering result, not an arbitrary finite-table increment or a restatement of a known sequence.
